content:
**Observations on test image:**
- Mango leaf showing large dark brownish-purple discoloration spreading across the right half and margins
- The dark patches appear superficial/coating-like rather than discrete lesions or tissue necrosis
- Leaf otherwise remains green and intact (no curling, tearing, or structural damage)

**Comparison with references:**
- **Sooty Mould**: Reference shows dark patches/black encrustations on green leaves — matches the superficial dark coating pattern in the test image closely
- **Powdery Mildew**: Shows white powdery spots — clearly does not match
- **Anthracnose**: Shows yellowed/brown leaves with margin/tip damage and lesions — does not match the test image pattern

The dark, spreading, superficial discoloration without tissue destruction is characteristic of Sooty Mould — fungal growth on honeydew secretions coating the leaf surface.

This pattern matches the sooty mould reference images showing dark encrustations on otherwise intact green leaves, and is inconsistent with anthracnose (which shows tip/margin lesions on yellowed leaves) or powdery mildew (white powdery coating)."}
